title: Bilirubin–albumin coupling gives a small conditional FEV1 prediction gain but fails a stable cross-cycle criterion
abstract: We tested a centered log-bilirubin–albumin product beyond nonlinear additive laboratory and conventional lung-function predictors. In 3,766 NHANES 2007–08 adults, fivefold MSE worsened by27.38mL². Frozen prediction in 4,165 separately sampled 2009–10 adults reduced FEV1 RMSE from455.543 to455.269mL. Target-only paired95% interval for delta MSE was[-488.57,-17.46]mL², but a joint source-refit/target stratified-PSU interval crossed zero[-1060.58,+192.11]. The source coefficient opposed the anticipated sign. Thus the registered stable-improvement criterion failed despite the small conditional target gain. This is cross-cycle testing under a shared survey protocol, not independent clinical-study validation or evidence of free-bilirubin physiology.
